translations.text: Bloodshed comes from the quarrelling of the proud, and their abuse is painful to hear.
Whoever reveals a secret destroys trust and will not find a friend suited to himself.
Love your friend and trust him. If you reveal his secrets, do not look back to him any more.
For as a man destroys his enemy, so you have destroyed the friendship of your neighbour.
Like a bird you have let go from your hands, you cannot bring it back.
Do not chase after him, for he has gone far from you. He has escaped like a gazelle from a snare.
For a wound can be bound up, and after abuse there can be reconciliation. But whoever reveals a secret has cut off hope.
Whoever winks with his eye is plotting evil, and whoever sees it will keep away from him.
To your face the enemy will make his mouth sweet, and he will win your admiration with his words. But in the end he will twist his mouth and twist your words [?].
There are many sins that I have hated, but I have compared none of them to this, and the Lord too has hated them.
Whoever throws a stone straight up will have it fall back on his own head, and a treacherous wound multiplies wounds [?].
Whoever digs a pit for his neighbour will fall into it himself, and whoever sets a trap will be caught in it himself.
Whoever piles up evil against his neighbour will have it roll back onto himself, and he will not know where the evil came from.
Mockery and insolent reproach belong to the proud, and vengeance lies in wait for them like a lion.
Those who rejoice at the fall of the righteous will be caught in a trap, and pain will wear them away until the day they die.
Enmity and anger are also a great abomination, and sinful men are carried away by them.
Whoever seeks retribution will meet it from God, and his sins will be utterly worn away [?].
Forgive your neighbour his offence. Then, when you pray, your sins will be forgiven you.
If a man keeps malice against another man, how then can he ask the Lord for mercy?
If that man has no mercy on someone like himself, how then can he ask forgiveness for his own sins?
He himself is only flesh, yet he knows how to keep up enmity. Who else will show mercy for his sins?
Remember the time of the end and put an end to enmity. Think about death, and quickly hold to the commandments.
Remember the commandments and do not bear enmity toward your neighbour. Think about the covenant of the Most High, and put wickedness away from you.
Keep away from strife, and your sins will become fewer, for the anger of a hot-tempered man stirs up strife.
A sinful man upsets friends and stirs up division among those who live in peace.
